question: How will the stopping potential change if the frequency of incident radiation is increased, keeping the metal surface unchanged? Justify your answer.

options.A: The stopping potential decreases because higher frequency decreases photon energy.
options.B: The stopping potential remains unchanged because the metal surface is unchanged.
options.C: The stopping potential depends only on intensity, so increasing frequency has no effect.
options.D: For the same metal, $eV_0=h\nu-\phi_0$. Increasing $\nu$ increases $K_{\max}$, so the stopping potential $V_0$ increases.
